In everyday life, this means: The base will hasten to sell themselves as soon as a calamity has befallen them. For what else are they fitted ?
Make it real today: Is this jewelled female a celestial, a choice peahen, or a human being ? My mind is perplexed
Bring the idea home: This female beauty returning my looks is like a celestial maiden coming with an army to contend against me
A practical reading: I never knew before what is called Yama; I see it now; it is the eyes that carry on a great fight with (the help of) female qualities
When life tests this: These eyes that seem to kill those who look at them are as it were in hostilities with this feminine simplicity
In everyday life, this means: Is it Yama, (a pair of) eyes or a hind ?- Are not all these three in the looks of this maid ?
Make it real today: Her eyes will cause (me) no trembling sorrow, if they are properly hidden by her cruel arched eyebrows
Bring the idea home: The cloth that covers the firm bosom of this maiden is (like) that which covers the eyes of a rutting elephant
A practical reading: On her bright brow alone is destroyed even that power of mine that used to terrify the most fearless
When life tests this: Of what use are other jewels to her who is adorned with modesty, and the meek looks of a hind ?
In everyday life, this means: Unlike boiled honey which yields delight only when it is drunk, love gives pleasure even when looked at
Make it real today: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof
Bring the idea home: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace)
A practical reading: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love
When life tests this: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently
In everyday life, this means: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles
Make it real today: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood
Bring the idea home: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers
A practical reading: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me
When life tests this: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers
In everyday life, this means: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers)
Make it real today: The (simultaneous) enjoyment of the five senses of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch can only be found with bright braceleted (women)
Bring the idea home: The remedy for a disease is always something different (from it); but for the disease caused by this jewelled maid, she is herself the cure
A practical reading: Can the lotus-eyed Vishnu's heaven be indeed as sweet to those who delight to sleep in the delicate arms of their beloved ?
When life tests this: From whence has she got this fire that burns when I withdraw and cools when I approach ?
In everyday life, this means: Each varied form of joy the soul can wish is found
Make it real today: The shoulders of this fair one are made of ambrosia, for they revive me with pleasure every time I embrace them

Bring the idea home: The embraces of a gold-complexioned beautiful female are as pleasant as to dwell in one's own house and live by one's own (earnings) after distributing (a portion of it in charity)
A practical reading: To ardent lovers sweet is the embrace that cannot be penetrated even by a breath of breeze
When life tests this: Love quarrel, reconciliation and intercourse - these are the advantages reaped by those who marry for lust
In everyday life, this means: As (one's) ignorance is discovered the more one learns, so does repeated intercourse with a welladorned female (only create a desire for more)

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: Make it real today: May you flourish, O Anicham! you have a delicate nature But my beloved is more delicate than you

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: Bring the idea home: O my soul, fancying that flowers which are seen by many can resemble her eyes, you become confused at the sight of them

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: A practical reading: The complexion of this bamboo-shouldered one is that of a shoot; her teeth, are pearls; her breath,

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: When life tests this: If the blue lotus could see, it would stoop and look at the ground saying, "I can never resemble the eyes of this excellent jewelled one."

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: In everyday life, this means: No merry drums will be beaten for the (tender) waist of her who has adorned herself with the anicham without having removed its stem

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: Make it real today: The stars have become confused in their places not being able to distinguish between the moon and the maid's countenance

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: Bring the idea home: Could there be spots in the face of this maid like those in the bright full moon ?

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: A practical reading: If you can indeed shine like the face of women, flourish, O moon, for then would you be worth loving ?

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: When life tests this: O moon, if you wish to resemble the face of her whose eyes are like (these) flowers, do not appear so as to be seen by all

t: Practicing The Praise of her Beauty
m: In everyday life, this means: The anicham and the feathers of the swan are to the feet of females, like the fruit of the (thorny) Nerunji

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: Make it real today: The water which oozes from the white teeth of this soft speeched damsel is like a mixture of milk and honey

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: Bring the idea home: The love between me and this damsel is like the union of body and soul

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: A practical reading: O you image in the pupil (of my eye)! depart; there is no room for (my) fair-browed beloved

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: When life tests this: My fair-jewelled one resembles the living soul (when she is in union with me), the dying soul when she leaves me

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: In everyday life, this means: If I had forgotten her who has bright battling eyes, I would have remembered (thee); but I never forget her (Thus says he to her maid)

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: Make it real today: My lover would not depart from mine eyes; even if I wink, he would not suffer (from pain); he is so ethereal

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: Bring the idea home: My lover abides in my eyes, I will not even paint them, for he would (then) have to conceal himself

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: A practical reading: My lover is in my heart, I am afraid of eating (anything) hot, for I know it would pain him

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: When life tests this: I will not wink, knowing that if I did, my lover would hide himself; and for this reason, this town says, he is unloving

t: Practicing Declaration of Love"s special Excellence
m: In everyday life, this means: My lover dwells in my heart with perpetual delight; but the town says he is unloving and (therefore) dwells afar
Make it real today: To those who after enjoyment of sexual pleasure suffer (for want of more), there is no help so efficient as the palmyra horse
Bring the idea home: Having got rid of shame, the suffering body and soul save themselves on the palmyra horse
A practical reading: Modesty and manliness were once my own; now, my own is the palmyra horse that is ridden by the lustful
When life tests this: The raft of modesty and manliness, is, alas, carried-off by the strong current of lust
In everyday life, this means: She with the small garland-like bracelets has given me the palmyra horse and the sorrow that is endured at night
Make it real today: Mine eyes will not close in sleep on your mistress's account; even at midnight will I think of mounting the palmyra horse
Bring the idea home: There is nothing so noble as the womanly nature that would not ride the palmyra horse, though plunged a sea of lust
A practical reading: Even the Lust (of women) transgresses its secrecy and appears in public, forgetting that they are too chaste and liberal (to be overcome by it)
When life tests this: And thus, in public ways, perturbed will rove
In everyday life, this means: Even strangers laugh (at us) so as to be seen by us, for they have not suffered

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: Make it real today: My precious life is saved by the raise of rumour, and this, to my good luck no others are aware of

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: Bring the idea home: Not knowing the value of her whose eyes are like flowers this town has got up a rumour about me

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: A practical reading: Will I not get a rumour that is known to the (whole) town ? For what I have not got is as if I had got it (already)

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: When life tests this: Rumour increases the violence of my passion; without it it would grow weak and waste away

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: In everyday life, this means: Drinking liquor is delightful (to one) whenever one is in mirth, so is lust delightful to me whenever it is the subject of rumour

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: Make it real today: It was but a single day that I looked on (my lover); but the rumour thereof has spread like the seizure of the moon by the serpent

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: Bring the idea home: This malady (of lust) is manured by the talk of women and watered by the (harsh) words of my mother

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: A practical reading: To say that one could extinguish passion by rumour is like extinguishing fire with ghee

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: When life tests this: When the departure of him who said "fear not" has put me to shame before others, why need I be ashamed of scandal

t: Practicing The Announcement of the Rumour
m: In everyday life, this means: The rumour I desire is raised by the town (itself); and my lover would if desired consent (to my following him)
Make it real today: If it is not departure, tell me; but if it is your speedy return, tell it to those who would be alive then
Bring the idea home: His very look was once pleasing; but (now) even intercourse is painful through fear of separation
A practical reading: Even the lover who understands (everything) may at times depart, confidence is hardly possible
When life tests this: If he who bestowed his love and said "fear not" should depart, will it be the fault of those who believed in (his) assuring words ?
In everyday life, this means: If you would save (my life), delay the departure of my destined (husband); for if he departs, intercourse will become impossible
Make it real today: Is hard, when he could stand, and of departure speak to me
Bring the idea home: Do not the rings that begin to slide down my fingers forebode the separation of my lord ?
A practical reading: Painful is it to live in a friendless town; but far more painful is it to part from one's lover
When life tests this: Fire burns when touched; but, like the sickness of love, can it also burn when removed ?
In everyday life, this means: If there were many indeed that can consent to the impossible, kill their pain, endure separation and yet continue to live afterwards
Make it real today: I would hide this pain from others; but it (only) swells like a spring to those who drain it
Bring the idea home: I cannot conceal this pain, nor can I relate it without shame to him who has caused it
A practical reading: (Both) lust and shame, with my soul for their shoulder pole balance themselves on a body that cannot bear them
When life tests this: There is indeed a flood of lust; but there is no raft of safety to cross it with
In everyday life, this means: What will they prove when angry tempests lower?
Make it real today: The pleasure of lust is (as great as) the sea; but the pain of lust is far greater
Bring the idea home: I have swam across the terrible flood of lust, but have not seen its shore; even at midnight I am alone; still I live
A practical reading: The night which graciously lulls to sleep all living creatures, has me alone for her companion
When life tests this: The long nights of these days are far more cruel than the heartless one who is torturing me
In everyday life, this means: Could mine eyes travel like my thoughts to the abode (of my absent lord), they would not swim in this flood of tears
Make it real today: This incurable malady has been caused by my eyes which showed (him) to me, why should they now weep for (him)
Bring the idea home: The dyed eyes that (then) looked without foresight, why should they now endure sorrow, without feeling sharply (their own fault)
A practical reading: They themselves looked eagerly (on him) and now they weep. Is not this to be laughed at ?
When life tests this: These painted eyes have caused me a lasting mortal disease; and now they can weep no more, the tears having dried up
In everyday life, this means: Mine eyes have caused me a lust that is greater than the sea and (they themselves) endure the torture of sleeplessness
Make it real today: The eyes that have given me this disease have themselves been seized with this (suffering) Oh! I am much delighted
Bring the idea home: The eyes that became tender and gazed intently on him, may they suffer so much as to dry up the fountain of their tears
A practical reading: He is indeed here who loved me with his lips but not with his heart but mine eyes suffer from not seeing him
When life tests this: When he is away they do not sleep; when he is present they do not sleep; in either case, mine eyes endure unbearable agony
In everyday life, this means: It is not difficult for the people of this place to understand the secret of those whose eyes, like mine, are as it were beaten drums
Make it real today: I who (then) consented to the absence of my loving lord, to whom can I (now) relate the fact of my having turned sallow
Bring the idea home: Sallowness, as if proud of having been caused by him, would now ride on my person
A practical reading: He has taken (away) my beauty and modesty, and given me instead disease and sallowness
When life tests this: I think (of him); and what I speak about is but his excellence; still is there sallowness; and this is deceitful
In everyday life, this means: Just as my lover departed then, did not sallowness spread here on my person ?
Make it real today: Just as darkness waits for the failing light; so does sallowness wait for the laxity of my husband's intercourse
Bring the idea home: I who was in close embrace just turned aside and the moment I did so, sallowness came on me like something to be seized on
A practical reading: Besides those who say "she has turned sallow" there are none who say "he has forsaken her"
When life tests this: If he is clear of guilt who has conciliated me (to his departure) let my body suffer its due and turn sallow
In everyday life, this means: It would be good to be said of me that I have turned sallow, if friends do not reproach with unkindness him who pleased me (then)
Make it real today: The women who are beloved by those whom they love, have they have not got the stone-less fruit of sexual delight ?
Bring the idea home: The bestowal of love by the beloved on those who love them is like the rain raining (at the proper season) on those who live by it
A practical reading: The pride that says "we shall live" suits only those who are loved by their beloved (husbands)
When life tests this: Even those who are esteemed (by other women) are devoid of excellence, if they are not loved by their beloved
In everyday life, this means: He who is beloved by me, what will he do to me, if I am not beloved by him ?
Make it real today: Lust, like the weight of the KAVADI, pains if it lies in one end only but pleases if it is in both
Bring the idea home: Would not cupid who abides and contends in one party (only) witness the pain and sorrow (in that party)?
A practical reading: There is no one in the world so hard-hearted as those who can live without receiving (even) a kind word from their beloved
When life tests this: Though my beloved bestows no love on one, still are his words sweet to my ears
In everyday life, this means: Live, O my soul, would you who relate your great sorrow to strangers, try rather to fill up your own sea (of sorrow)
Make it real today: Sexuality is sweeter than liquor, because when remembered, it creates a most rapturous delight
Bring the idea home: Even to think of one's beloved gives one no pain Sexuality, in any degree, is always delightful
A practical reading: I feel as if I am going to sneeze but do not, and (therefore) my beloved is about to think (of me) but does not
When life tests this: He continues to abide in my soul, do I likewise abide in his ?
In everyday life, this means: He who has imprisoned me in his soul, is he ashamed to enter incessantly into mine
Make it real today: I live by remembering my (former) intercourse with him; if it were not so, how could I live ?
Bring the idea home: I have never forgotten (the pleasure); even to think of it burns my soul; could I live, if I should ever forget it ?
A practical reading: He will not be angry however much I may think of him; is it not so much the delight my beloved
When life tests this: My precious life is wasting away by thinking too much on the cruelty of him who said we were not different
In everyday life, this means: May you live, O Moon! Do not set, that I mine see him who has departed without quitting my soul

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: Make it real today: Where with shall I feast the dream which has brought me my dear one's messenger ?

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: Bring the idea home: If my fish-like painted eyes should, at my begging, close in sleep, I could fully relate my sufferings to my lord

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: A practical reading: My life lasts because in my dream I behold him who does not favour me in my waking hours

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: When life tests this: There is pleasure in my dream, because in it I seek and obtain him who does not visit me in my wakefulness

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: In everyday life, this means: I saw him in my waking hours, and then it was pleasant; I see him just now in my dream, and it is (equally) pleasant

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: Make it real today: Were there no such thing as wakefulness, my beloved (who visited me) in my dream would not depart from me

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: Bring the idea home: The cruel one who would not favour me in my wakefulness, what right has he to torture me in my dreams?

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: A practical reading: When I am asleep he rests on my shoulders, (but) when I awake he hastens into my soul

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: When life tests this: They who have no dear ones to behold in their dreams blame him who visits me not in my waking hours

t: Practicing The Visions of the Night
m: In everyday life, this means: The women of this place say he has forsaken me in my wakefulness I think they have not seen him visit me in my dreams
Make it real today: Live, O you evening are you (the former) evening? No, you are the season that slays (married) women
Bring the idea home: A long life to you, O dark evening! You are sightless Is your help-mate (also) as hard-hearted as mine
A practical reading: The evening that (once) came in with trembling and dimness (now) brings me an aversion for life and increasing sorrow
When life tests this: In the absence of my lover, evening comes in like slayers on the field of slaughter
In everyday life, this means: O eve, why art thou foe! thou dost renew my grief
Make it real today: Previous to my husband's departure, I know not the painful nature of evening
Bring the idea home: This malady buds forth in the morning, expands all day long and blossoms in the evening
A practical reading: The shepherd's flute now sounds as a fiery forerunner of night, and is become a weapon that slays (me)
When life tests this: When night comes on confusing (everyone's) mind, the (whole) town will lose its sense and be plunged in sorrow
In everyday life, this means: My (hitherto) unextinguished life is now lost in this bewildering night at the thought of him who has the nature of wealth
Make it real today: While we endure the unbearable sorrow, your eyes weep for him who is gone afar, and shun (the sight of) fragrant flowers
Bring the idea home: The discoloured eyes that shed tears profusely seem to betray the unkindness of our beloved
A practical reading: The shoulders that swelled on the day of our union (now) seem to announce our separation clearly (to the public)
When life tests this: In the absence of your consort, your shoulders having lost their former beauty and fulness, your bracelets of pure gold have become loose
In everyday life, this means: The (loosened) bracelets, and the shoulders from which the old beauty has faded, relate the cruelty of the pitiless one
Make it real today: I am greatly pained to hear you call him a cruel man, just because your shoulders are reduced and your bracelets loosened
Bring the idea home: Can you O my soul! gain glory by relating to the (so-called) cruel one the clamour of my fading shoulders?
A practical reading: When I once loosened the arms that were in embrace, the forehead of the gold-braceleted women turned sallow
When life tests this: When but a breath of breeze penetrated our embrace, her large cool eyes became sallow
In everyday life, this means: Was it at the sight of what the bright forehead had done that the sallowness of her eyes became sad?
Make it real today: O my soul, will you not think and tell me some medicine be it what it may, that can cure this incurable malady?
Bring the idea home: Is folly, fare thee well my heart!
A practical reading: O my soul! why remain (here) and suffer thinking (of him)? There are no lewd thoughts (of you) in him who has caused you this disease of sorrow
When life tests this: O my soul! take my eyes also with you, (if not), these would eat me up (in their desire) to see him
In everyday life, this means: O my soul! can he who loves not though he is beloved, be forsaken saying he hates me (now)?
Make it real today: O my soul! when you see the dear one who remove dislike by intercourse, you are displeased and continue to be so Nay, your displeasure is (simply) false
Bring the idea home: O my good soul, give up either lust or honour, as for me I can endure neither
A practical reading: You are a fool, O my soul! to go after my departed one, while you mourn that he is not kind enough to favour you
When life tests this: O my soul! to whom would you repair, while the dear one is within yourself?
In everyday life, this means: If I retain in my heart him who has left me without befriending me, I shall lose even the (inward) beauty that remains
Make it real today: The axe of lust can break the door of chastity which is bolted with the bolt of modesty
Bring the idea home: Even at midnight is my mind worried by lust, and this one thing, alas! is without mercy
A practical reading: I would conceal my lust, but alas, it yields not to my will but breaks out like a sneeze
When life tests this: I say I would be firm, but alas, my malady breaks out from its concealment and appears in public
In everyday life, this means: The dignity that would not go after an absent lover is not known to those who are sticken by love
Make it real today: The sorrow I have endured by desiring to go after my absent lover, in what way is it excellent?
Bring the idea home: I know nothing like shame when my beloved does from love (just) what is desired (by me)
A practical reading: Are not the enticing words of my trick-abounding roguish lover the weapon that breaks away my feminine firmness?
When life tests this: I said I would feign dislike and so went (away); (but) I embraced him the moment I say my mind began to unite with him!
In everyday life, this means: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat in the fire to say they can feign a strong dislike and remain so?
Make it real today: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail
Bring the idea home: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose
A practical reading: I still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide
When life tests this: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love
In everyday life, this means: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders
Make it real today: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow
Bring the idea home: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?
A practical reading: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening
When life tests this: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days
In everyday life, this means: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: Make it real today: Though you would conceal (your feelings), your painted eyes would not, for, transgressing (their bounds), they tell (me) something

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: Bring the idea home: Unusually great is the female simplicity of your maid whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders resemble the bamboo

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: A practical reading: There is something that is implied in the beauty of this woman, like the thread that is visible in a garland of gems

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: When life tests this: There is something in the unmatured smile of this maid like the fragrance that is contained in an unblossomed bud

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: In everyday life, this means: The well-meant departure of her whose bangles are tight-fitting contains a remedy that can cure my great sorrow

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: Make it real today: The embrace that fills me with comfort and gladness is capable of enduring (my former) sorrow and meditating on his want of love

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: Bring the idea home: My bracelets have understood before me the (mental) separation of him who rules the cool seashore

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: A practical reading: It was but yesterday my lover departed (from me); and it is seven days since my complexion turned sallow

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: When life tests this: She looked at her bracelets, her tender shoulders, and her feet; this was what she did there (significantly)

t: Practicing The Reading of the Signs
m: In everyday life, this means: To express their love-sickness by their eyes and resort to begging bespeaks more than ordinary female excellence
Make it real today: To please by thought and cheer by sight is peculiar, not to liquor but lust
Bring the idea home: If women have a lust that exceeds even the measure of the palmyra fruit, they will not desire (to feign) dislike even as much as the millet
A practical reading: Though my eyes disregard me and do what is pleasing to my husband, still will they not be satisfied unless they see him
When life tests this: My heart, forgetting all, could not its love restrain
In everyday life, this means: Like the eyes which see not the pencil that paints it, I cannot see my husband's fault (just) when I meet him
Make it real today: When I see my husband, I do not see any faults; but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but faults
Bring the idea home: Like those who leap into a stream which they know will carry them off, why should a wife feign dislike which she knows cannot hold out long?
A practical reading: O you rogue! your breast is to me what liquor is to those who rejoice in it, though it only gives them an unpleasant disgrace
When life tests this: Sexual delight is more delicate than a flower, and few are those who understand its real nature
In everyday life, this means: She once feigned dislike in her eyes, but the warmth of her embrace exceeded my own
Make it real today: O my soul! although you have seen how his soul stands by him, how is it you do not stand by me?
Bring the idea home: O my soul! although you have known him who does not love me, still do you go to him, saying "he will not be displeased."
A practical reading: O my soul! do you follow him at pleasure under the belief that the ruined have no friends?
When life tests this: O my soul! you would not first seem sulky and then enjoy (him); who then would in future consult you about such things?
In everyday life, this means: My soul fears when it is without him; it also fears when it is with him; it is subject to incessant sorrow
Make it real today: My mind has been (here) in order to eat me up (as it were) whenever I think of him in my solitude
Bring the idea home: I have even forgotten my modesty, having been caught in my foolish mind which is not dignified enough to forget him
A practical reading: My soul which clings to life thinks only of his (own) gain in the belief that it would be disgraceful for it to despise him
When life tests this: Who would help me out of one's distress, when one's own soul refuses help to one?
In everyday life, this means: It is hardly possible for strangers to behave like relations, when one's own soul acts like a stranger
Make it real today: Let us witness awhile his keen suffering; just feign dislike and embrace him not
Bring the idea home: A little dislike is like salt in proportion; to prolong it a little is like salt a little too much
A practical reading: For men not to embrace those who have feigned dislike is like torturing those already in agony
When life tests this: Not to reconcile those who have feigned dislike is like cutting a faded creeper at its root
In everyday life, this means: An increased shyness in those whose eyes are like flowers is beautiful even to good and virtuous husbands
Make it real today: Sexual pleasure, without prolonged and short-lived dislike, is like too ripe, and unripe fruit
Bring the idea home: The doubt as to whether intercourse would take place soon or not, creates a sorrow (even) in feigned dislike
A practical reading: What avails sorrow when I am without a wife who can understand the cause of my sorrow?
When life tests this: Like water in the shade, dislike is delicious only in those who love
In everyday life, this means: It is nothing but strong desire that makes her mind unite with me who can leave her to her own dislike
Make it real today: You are given to prostitution; all those who are born as womankind enjoy you with their eyes in an ordinary way I will not embrace you
